Crash-damaged console material — 2026-11-06

Generated using OpenAI's built-in image_gen tool for this project under the
user's request for a worn, scratched, crash-damaged console. No third-party
source image was used. Original preserved in output/crash-console-v78/.

Selected production asset: crashed-metal.webp, 1024 x 1024 RGB.
Normalization: Lanczos resize and WebP compression only. No aesthetic edits.
This is a material surface, not a panel mockup. Use behind code-native UI,
with shading over body-reading areas. Exact edge tiling is not guaranteed;
prefer cropped single-image surfaces or low-contrast repeated applications.

Final generation prompt (built-in mode):
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: square production material
texture for a crash-damaged science-fiction aircraft console UI. Create a
single continuous flat orthographic surface of dark charcoal-blue painted
aerospace metal. Clearly weathered: irregular silver scratches of varied
lengths, chipped blue-grey paint revealing dull metal, dense fine machining
grain, rubbed patches, a few small dull rusty oxidation freckles, oily soot
and dust trapped in grooves, several restrained long oblique gouges. It
should read as metal that survived a violent crash and years of handling.
Material colour stays graphite/navy, not bright steel. Soft flat even
lighting, albedo-like, no cast shadows, no vignette. Surface detail is organic
and irregular, with visible wear at 512-pixel scale and quiet areas between
scratch clusters. Entire square is just the material surface, edge-to-edge;
no bezel, panel boundary, bolts, seams, screens, labels, words, lettering,
numbers, symbols, UI controls, objects, scenery, perspective, watermark, or
frame. Prefer edges that repeat plausibly when used as a CSS texture.
Square 1024x1024 composition.

Companion code-native decoration authored for this project:
- impact-corner.svg: irregular metal fracture, soot and exposed edge detail.
- worn-rim.svg: transparent perimeter paint chips and rubbed metal edges.
Both remain non-interactive decoration; worn-rim stretches to each panel's
exact border so its chipped paint does not drift across the reading area.
